what_happened: Shipped a write-side rollback handler for an AI agent that trades real money. Walks decision chain MRU->LRU, idempotent, single Discord summary, daily rollback budget cap of 3.
why_content_worthy: Most AI agent demos handle the happy path. Almost nobody talks about REVERSIBLE REASONING — what does it mean for an AI agent to undo something it did? This is novel territory for AI-agents-handling-money specifically.

what_happened: Originally Friday 5/1 was the live cutover. Slipped to Tuesday 5/5 mid-day after env audit. Then scrapped Tuesday entirely in favor of graduation-gating: live happens when shadow accuracy >=0.90, pairs >=50, daily profit >=$1.
why_content_worthy: Calendar-driven cutovers ARE the wrong gate when you're shipping autonomous agents handling real capital. Most teams ship by calendar; the shadow-graduation pattern is genuinely better. This is a strong contrarian take.

what_happened: Codified the strategic principle: rent foundation models from Anthropic + Ollama; build the moat in orchestration + corpus + brains + shadows on top. Don't compete with frontier labs.
why_content_worthy: Builders are constantly asking 'should I build my own model?' The answer is almost always no, and the WHY is well-articulated here. Strong contrarian-but-correct take that helps people stop wasting time.

what_happened: Designed a 5-layer agent OS: L0 Thomas (sole approval) / L1 Boss (orchestrator) / L2 Infrastructure (router, observability) / L3 Departments (CMO, Operations, Sales) / L4 Projects (TENx10, DSR, MHP) / L5 Shadow Team. Each layer has rollback semantics and a unified observability contract.
why_content_worthy: Most agent designs are flat or 2-layer. A 5-layer hierarchy with explicit per-layer rollback + Thomas-as-only-approval-point is genuinely different and addresses real failure modes (over-permissioning, faceless automation).
